description: Livestock semen quality as negative control for CSLI analysis. Unlike human/dog sperm, bull and boar semen quality is STABLE or IMPROVING over decades.
rationale: If environmental EDCs alone drove reproductive decline, livestock in the same chemical environment should also decline. They do not — genetic selection and controlled breeding maintain or improve semen quality. This supports EMF-specific mechanisms: livestock are typically housed in rural areas with lower RF exposure and/or in metal-framed barns that attenuate RF fields.

sources.citation: Wahl RL, Reif JS. Temporal trends in bull semen quality: a comparative model for human health? Environ Res. 2009;109(3):273-280.
sources.conclusion: If EDCs were the cause, continued decline would be expected. Instead, quality rose in the latter period. Source of initial decline unknown.

sources.citation: Karoui S et al. Time trends, environmental factors and genetic basis of semen traits collected in Holstein bulls under commercial conditions. Anim Reprod Sci. 2011;124(1-2):40-50.
sources.conclusion: No systematic time trends observed except post-thawing motility, which increased due to improved freezing-thawing protocols. Heritability estimates moderate (0.16-0.22).

sources.citation: Hensel B, Henneberg S, Schröter F, Hürland M, Osmers JH, Geissendörfer S, Lautner M, Jung M, Schulze M. Temporal trends in porcine and bovine semen characteristics: A retrospective long-term analysis of semen production data. Anim Reprod Sci. 2025;286:108093.
sources.note: Full text not accessible at extraction time. Article confirms long-term retrospective analysis of both species' semen production data. Awaiting institutional access for detailed parameter trends.

bovine.key_finding: No systematic decline. Brief dip 1970-1985 reversed. Post-thaw motility improved via technology.

porcine.note: Hensel 2025 provides the definitive long-term porcine dataset. Based on search results, genetic selection and AI management maintain or improve boar semen quality.

contrast_with_sentinel_species.human: Sperm concentration declined 51.6% from 1973-2018, accelerating post-2000 (Levine 2023)
contrast_with_sentinel_species.interpretation: Livestock under genetic selection and controlled rural environments do NOT show the reproductive decline seen in human, dog, and horse populations exposed to urban/suburban RF-EMF levels.
